result.title: UACR: Uncertainty-Aware Collaborative Routing for Explainable Industrial Anomaly Inspection
result.summary: Industrial anomaly inspection requires not only accurate anomaly discrimination but also trustworthy explanations for operators, while satisfying the strict latency constraints of online inspection. Existing methods, however, typically apply a fixed computational path to all samples, making it difficult to strike a good balance among detection accuracy, inference efficiency, and interpretability. To address this issue, we propose UACR, an uncertainty-aware collaborative routing framework for explainable industrial anomaly inspection. UACR aims to deliver reliable anomaly decisions together with operator-facing explanations under the online inspection budget, while adaptively allocating computation so that ambiguous cases receive deeper scrutiny. The framework consists of two stages. Stage I, Offline Training and Routing Hyperparameter Search, learns the anomaly inspection modules and calibrates the uncertainty estimator that drives routing. Stage II, Uncertainty-Aware Adaptive Routing, collaboratively dispatches each input across inspection paths according to its estimated uncertainty. Experimental results on multiple public datasets show that UACR achieves over 5.16% improvement in accuracy compared to the baseline method, while reducing latency by over 31.5%. It also enhances the interpretability of industrial detection by over 15%.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 UACR 两阶段框架用于工业异常检测：先离线训练检测模块并校准不确定性估计器，再按样本不确定性将输入协同路由到不同检测路径，在在线时延预算下兼顾精度、效率与可解释性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按不确定性分配计算、疑难样本走更深路径」的路由与校准机制，可供核查是否用于 LVR 中动态计算分配与停止决策的触发信号设计，但应用域与推理状态表示距离较远。
